strategic_themes.title: Lift qualified audit opinion (Grant Thornton UK LLP)
strategic_themes.rationale: External auditor issued a qualified opinion on 2024/25 statements. Direct: PSAA scale fee normalisation. Indirect: lifting governance flag reduces borrowing-cost premium. Manual read of audit report needed to itemise qualification reason — once known, target single-cycle remediation.

strategic_themes.title: Agency / locum staff demand reduction (£4M concentrated)
strategic_themes.rationale: £4M of agency-staff spend across 1 master vendors. Top: MATRIX SCM LTD (£4M). Standard transformation: cap agency premium at 20% above substantive rate, workforce-plan permanent conversion (6-9 month payback), regional bank pool, open-book master-vendor margins. CIPFA experience: 8-15% reduction in 12-18 months.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of HR + Director of Finance + S151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Energy procurement via CCS / LASER / NEPO frameworks (£3M baseline)
strategic_themes.rationale: £3M utility spend across 2 suppliers. Top: NPOWER (ELECTRICITY) LTD (£2M), CORONA ENERGY RETAIL 4 LTD (£1M). Crown Commercial RM6306 + LASER / NEPO consortium flex purchase typically saves 4-8% vs direct supplier contracts on a 3-yr horizon. Plus solar PV self-generation on council estate (7-9 yr payback) + DESNZ Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme grants up to 100% capex on heat pump conversion.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of Property + Sustainability Lead + S151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Treasury management + borrowing cost optimisation (CFR proxy £321M)
strategic_themes.rationale: Annual revenue £402M implies indicative CFR c. £321M. Standard levers: internal borrowing from earmarked reserves, PWLB Certainty Rate trade, MMF counterparty restructuring, LGPS Property Investment Pool inclusion. 10-30bp saving on external debt typical from a fresh review.

strategic_themes.title: LGPS employer contribution opportunity (2025 triennial valuation cycle)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative pay bill £161M × c. 22% employer contribution rate = £35M annual employer contribution. Most LGPS funds materially over-funded post-2022 (returns 2022-25 averaged 7-10% pa vs 3-4% discount-rate assumption). 2025 triennial valuation typically yields 2-4pp employer-rate reduction over 2026-2029. Confirm with administering authority + actuary.

strategic_themes.title: Fees, charges + traded-services income optimisation (£40M base)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative fees & charges + traded-services income c. 10% of revenue = £40M. Standard levers: annual CPI uplift discipline, full-cost-recovery audit on discretionary services (parking, planning, licensing, sports, adult learning, property hire), commercial pricing on traded services. LGA experience: 5-15% income uplift sustainable over 2-3 years.

strategic_themes.title: Insurance retention + premium review (£0.4M premium estimate)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative insurance premium £0.4M (10bp of revenue). Standard 3-5 yr renewal cycle. Levers: tender via IPG / RM Partners (10-25% premium reduction typical), retention review (increase excess + build risk-fund reserve). London-borough cohort average 12% premium reduction at last tender.

strategic_themes.title: Contracts Finder portfolio review (29 notices; 0 contracts at £10M+ ceiling)
strategic_themes.rationale: Contracts Finder data: 29 notices (28 awarded, £10M aggregate ADVERTISED CEILING value, 0% SME). IMPORTANT: advertised contract value is a CEILING set to avoid retender risk under PCR 2015 Reg.72 / Procurement Act 2023 s.31 — actual spend through the awardee is typically 30-70% of ceiling, with some off-contract ledger spend permitted within the 50%/50% modification limits. 0 contracts at £10M+ ceiling totalling £0M (ceiling, NOT spend) — top 3: . Matched against ledger: GB-St Helens: TPPL St Helens Borough Council NEPO  — ceiling £0.1M, actual ledger spend with awardee £57.0M; GB-St Helens: TPPL St Helens Borough Council NEPO  — ceiling £0.1M, actual ledger spend with awardee £57.0M; GB-St Helens: TPPL St Helens Borough Council NEPO  — ceiling £0.0M, actual ledger spend with awardee £0.2M. Aggregate identified actual spend £118M. SME-awarded share 0% is below the Procurement Reform 2023 / PPN 03/24 ambition (33% SME share by value). Standard procurement-data savings levers (% of ACTUAL ledger spend, not ceiling): (a) modification-history scrutiny under PCR 2015 Reg.72, (b) Procurement Act 2023 s.31 contract change notice review, (c) re-tender benchmark vs CCS framework rates on next renewal. 2-8% on actual spend through major contracts is a defensible upper bound.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Head of Procurement + Cabinet Member + Section 151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Refund / credit-note management + contract dispute resolution (£43M, 2,696 rows)
strategic_themes.rationale: 2,696 negative-amount rows totalling £43M — refunds, credit notes, contract reversals. Volume signals correct ledger capture, but proactive levers exist: (a) contract management review on top recurring refund counterparties, (b) duplicate-payment pre-detection, (c) energy-bill credit-management automation. Typical 5-10% reduction in refund volume + faster reconciliation = 10-30bp net cash improvement.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Head of Procurement + Internal Audit + Treasury

strategic_themes.title: Rebuild general reserves to ≥4 months (Low → Adequate)
strategic_themes.rationale: Reserves at 3.1 months (Low per CIPFA Resilience benchmark). Direction: declining. A 4-month minimum is the CIPFA / S151 prudence floor; below this triggers external auditor VFM concern and elevates s.114 risk.

strategic_themes.title: Audit + recover £5M in flagged duplicate-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE forensic flagged £5M across 1,558 groups of likely duplicates. Industry recovery norm 5-15% via duplicate-detection software (AP Forensics, FISCAL, Oracle Concur). Lloyds Bank Commercial Card analysis typical for spot-check sample of 100 highest-confidence matches.

strategic_themes.title: Investigate £13M in flagged split-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE flagged £13M across 0 split-payment instances. Split payments often indicate (a) below-procurement-threshold ledger fragmentation circumventing PCR 2015 Reg.4 contract-value-aggregation rule; or (b) legitimate sub-line invoice splits. Sample audit + reclassify; misuse triggers Reg. 99 challenge exposure.
